summary: Finish the R20-R24 extraction by strangling the forwarder layer out one collaborator at a time, smallest first, in twenty-three commits that are each provably green on their own. The opus skeleton survived both refutation passes best (rubric 4/4/5/4/4 and 4/5/5/5/4, the only variant no reviewer called unexecutable) and is kept: add-accessor -> migrate production -> migrate tests -> delete-forwarders, because that shape leaves a DURABLE RESTING STATE after every commit — the tree compiles with both paths present, so a stalled or reverted migration never strands a caller. The measured facts that shape it, re-verified at HEAD for this synthesis: store.svelte.ts is 3,630 lines; the five controllers are constructed once each as private fields (store.svelte.ts:386 sectionsCtl, :481 monitor, :490 controllerTest, :519 showsCtl, :805 midi); ~74 members are single-statement forwarders; and ~580 store-qualified call sites live in 27 files of which ~460 are in TEST files. That ratio is the whole risk story — the migration is 80% test churn, and test churn is exactly where a green suite stops being evidence, because the cheapest way to make a retargeted test pass is to weaken it. Both reviewers landed the attack that neither the opus nor the sonnet nor the fable diff gates could actually detect a weakened assertion (opus's S12 filter can never even pass), so every test-retarget commit now carries a RENAME-NORMALISED DIFF gate: sed the accessor rename over the pre-image and require a byte-empty diff, which is a mechanical proof that the only change is the accessor path. Three rival directions were tried and refuted, and this plan takes their refutations as constraints rather than re-litigating them. sonnet's DeviceLinkStore/LibraryStore wrapper facades were killed for recreating the exact one-adapter seam the initiative exists to delete, so the controllers are published DIRECTLY on TriggerLab. sonnet's S10 AuthoringStore — ~3,000 LOC across ~100 files in one commit with no resting state — was killed by both reviewers, so the authoring-document seam is not attempted here; instead S23 emits a tracked follow-on initiative record, because the other landed attack was that divergent-change-0002 otherwise closes with no owner. fable's un-export of the five *Host interfaces was killed on verified evidence: store.svelte.ts:397 and :538 `satisfies` those types, so un-exporting them would delete real static shape checking on the exact literals that wire the controllers — the Hosts stay exported, and S14 instead converts each from a hypothetical seam into a used one by constructing a controller against a stub host with no store at all, which is the evidence speculative-generality-0001 actually demanded. fable's deletion of canConnect/canReconnect was killed for churning 53 test call sites in the same commit as a positional-to-named transposition, so they survive as two-line sugar over the new WireEnds shape.

design.title: Pin the store's public surface with an inventory + size ratchet test
design.intent: Nothing today can tell you whether a refactor removed a member, moved one, or quietly added one. Create apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.surface.test.ts which constructs the store the same way every other store suite does — `new TriggerLab(fakeClient)` with the MemStorage localStorage beforeEach/afterEach pair copied from store.shows.test.ts:58-64 — computes the sorted union of `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(store))` (Svelte 5 compiles class `$state`/`$derived` fields to prototype accessors, so this captures them) and `Object.keys(store)`, filters out `constructor` and names starting with `_`, and asserts deep-equality against a checked-in `EXPECTED_MEMBERS` array in the same file. Also assert `EXPECTED_MEMBERS.length <= MEMBER_CAP` and that `readFileSync` line count of store.svelte.ts is `<= LOC_CAP`, both seeded from the values this step MEASURES (the plan's 397 members / 3,630 LOC are pre-measurements to be replaced by whatever the instrument actually reports). REPAIR (opus reviewer, landed): the default constructor at store.svelte.ts:876-879 builds a real `WSClient({ pin: readStoredPin(), hostToken: readHostToken() })` and opens a socket — a bare `new TriggerLab()` would make the one instrument the entire plan's parity evidence hangs off the one network-touching, flaky test in the suite. The fake client is not optional here.
design.verification: The new test passes at HEAD; record the measured EXPECTED_MEMBERS.length and LOC in the commit message. Prove it bites: temporarily add `get __probe() { return 1; }` to TriggerLab and confirm the test FAILS naming `__probe`; remove it. Prove it is hermetic: run the file alone with the network unavailable and confirm it passes and opens no socket (no WSClient construction in the test's own stack). `pnpm gates` green at 2,968 + the new cases.
design.reverses: Delete the single new file; it is referenced by nothing.

design.title: Tracer: publish ControllerTest, delete its 3 forwarders
design.intent: Smallest collaborator, 4 production call sites — the cheapest possible proof that the whole pattern works. In store.svelte.ts change `private readonly controllerTest = new ControllerTest({...})` (verified at :490) to `readonly controllerTest = ...` — DROP the `private`, do not add a same-named getter, which would be a duplicate class member and a compile error (this is the landed attack against fable's S1/S2/S3). Delete the three forwarders `get controllerTakeover()`, `setControllerTestData()`, `backToLive()`. Retarget: `store.controllerTakeover` -> `store.controllerTest.takeover` in OutputPill.svelte and PatchControllerInspector.svelte; `store.setControllerTestData(p)` -> `store.controllerTest.setTestData(p)` and `store.backToLive()` -> `store.controllerTest.backToLive()` in PatchControllerInspector.svelte; plus the ~10 hits in store.controller.test.ts. Note the controller member is `setTestData`, not `setControllerTestData` — the forwarder renamed it. STANDING CONSTRAINT for S3-S13, from the landed attack on fable: the five `*ControllerHost` interfaces STAY EXPORTED. store.svelte.ts:397 and :538 use them as `satisfies` constraints on the inline host literals; un-exporting them forces deleting those clauses, which silently removes excess-property and shape checking on the exact objects that wire the controllers. That is a real static-parity loss traded for an export-count cosmetic. S14 answers the Host half of speculative-generality-0001 instead, by making the seams used.
design.verification: `pnpm gates` green. store.surface.test.ts's EXPECTED_MEMBERS diff shows exactly three removals (controllerTakeover, setControllerTestData, backToLive) and zero additions — `controllerTest` was already an own-key, so dropping `private` adds no member. `rg -n 'satisfies ControllerTestHost' apps/web/src` still returns store.svelte.ts. `pnpm ui-shot patch-controller top-bar --strict` matches the S2 baseline: the LOUD test-pattern takeover banner still renders and the OutputPill still shows the takeover state.
design.reverses: `git revert` this one commit. Nothing else references `store.controllerTest.*` yet.

Retarget to `store.midi.learnTarget` / `.devices` / `.available` / `.unavailableReason` / `.startLearn()` / `.cancelLearn()` across PatchZoneInspector, TriggerSourceInspector, CcNodeInspector, DrumZonesList, AppSettingsDialog, store.cc.test.ts and store.echo-gate.test.ts. REPAIR (fable reviewer, landed): the opus variant's stated precondition 'still zero store-internal uses' is FALSE and is struck. There are five genuine internal, non-forwarder uses that must NOT be retargeted and are unaffected because the field keeps its name — `this.midi.openInput(...)` at :979, `this.midi.release()` at :1016, `this.midi.applyNoteLearn(...)` at :1065 and :1467, `this.midi.applyCcLearn(...)` at :1078. design.verification: `pnpm gates` green. EXPECTED_MEMBERS diff: exactly six removals, zero additions. `grep -c 'this\.midi\.' apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.svelte.ts` must drop from 11 to exactly 5, and each survivor must be one of :979/:1016/:1065/:1078/:1467 — that is the mechanical check that the forwarders went and the real internal uses stayed. `pnpm ui-shot midi-learn-trigger-source midi-learn-drum-zones midi-learn-cc-node patch-zone-inspector settings-dialog --strict` matches the S2 baseline; this is the ONLY evidence for these five components, none of which has a unit test. design.title: Retarget the test consumers of the 18 section forwarders (rename-normalised diff gate)
design.intent: The ~97 test hits across store.sections/store.looks/store.echo-gate/store.songs/store.graphs.test.ts and apps/web/src/lib/app/setlist.test.ts move to `store.arrangement.*`. This is deliberately its own commit because it is the step where a green suite is weakest evidence: retargeted tests are the cheapest thing in the repo to accidentally weaken. REPAIR (both reviewers, landed): the substring `rg -v` whitelist the opus variant proposed CANNOT detect a weakened assertion — every retargeted line necessarily contains the new accessor substring, so an edit anywhere else on that line (`toBe(3)` -> `toBe(2)`) is invisible, and equal per-file numstat is preserved by any 1-for-1 line edit. Replace it with a RENAME-NORMALISED DIFF, which is a proof rather than a heuristic: write the exact old-name -> new-name mapping into a checked-in `scripts/rename-gate.sh` invocation, apply it with sed to the PRE-IMAGE of each touched file (`git show <base>:<file>`), and require `diff` against the post-image to be byte-empty. Prove the gate bites before relying on it: hand-edit one expected value on an already-retargeted line and confirm the gate fails; revert the probe.

Land it green at HEAD against the existing classes. This is the parity contract S16 must not move.

behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: A green suite does NOT prove parity in five named places. (1) Component coverage: 19 of the 22 .svelte files this plan edits have zero test importing them — TopBar, ObjectsView, SectionsView, GraphsDock, SectionColumn, PerformView, SectionGraphRow, SectionInspector, PatchControllerInspector, OutputPill, SaveIndicator, TriggerGraphView, DrumZonesList, CcNodeInspector, TriggerSourceInspector, PatchZoneInspector, LibrarySongRow, LibraryRefRow, AppSettingsDialog. For those, svelte-check proves the accessor path resolves and ui-shot proves the surface renders with a clean console; NEITHER proves interaction. What replaces the missing tests is the diff shape itself: every edit to those files in S3-S13 is a pure accessor-path rename with no logic touched, so the reviewable claim is 'this diff contains only renames' — checkable by a human in minutes and, for the test files, now mechanically checkable by the rename-normalised gate. (2) The MIDI device half — MidiController.openInput/release against real WebMIDI — has no coverage in any environment; S4 does not touch it (no forwarder covered it, and the five genuine internal uses keep their name) but the five inspectors that arm MIDI-learn are proven only by svelte-check plus a hardware pass. (3) QuotaExceededError is browser-specific: Safari private mode throws on the first setItem, Chrome at roughly 5MB. S21's stub proves the code path, not the trigger, so 'the indicator goes red when storage is genuinely full' rests on one manual Safari-private-mode pass. S22's error state is NEW behaviour by design, not preserved behaviour — there is nothing to be parity-checked against, only the happy path to be left intact. (4) Svelte 5 rune reactivity through the new `store.library.*` path: a getter returning a controller whose fields are `$state` is the same proxy graph, but no test asserts fine-grained re-render behaviour; the replacement evidence is the ui-shot captures and the named live passes, which exercise real reactive subscriptions. (5) divergent-change-0002's actual claim — that unrelated concerns STOP converging on one file — is a claim about FUTURE commits and is unprovable by any run today. The ratchet in S1/S23 is an honest substitute that prevents regrowth rather than demonstrating separation; the only real evidence will be re-running the churn histogram after another ~50 commits, which is out of this initiative's reach and is why S23 emits a tracked follow-on record rather than a comment.

rollback_strategy: Twenty-three commits, each independently `git revert`-able, reverted in reverse landing order. The plan is deliberately shaped so there are DURABLE RESTING STATES: after S6 and after S10 the tree carries BOTH the forwarders and the new collaborator accessor, so a migration abandoned mid-way (S7 or S11 landed, S9/S13 not) is a perfectly shippable tree — the forwarders simply have fewer callers. That property is why the strangler shape survived both refutation passes while sonnet's single-commit AuthoringStore did not. Reverting a delete step (S9, S13) restores the forwarders and still compiles because the callers already use the new path; reverting a retarget step (S7, S8, S11, S12) still compiles because the forwarders were never removed. The only unsafe sequence is reverting S6 or S10 while a later step is still in, so those two revert LAST; a revert of S9/S13 meant to be permanent should be followed by reverting the matching retarget commits, not left half-way. Six steps stand alone and revert at any time: S14 and S15 and S19 (test-only additions), S16 (library-sync unification — the generic, both deletions and the construction sites in one commit), S17+S18 (shell, no overlap with any store step), and S20 (WireEnds — a signature and all its call sites in one commit, so a partial revert is impossible by construction). S22 is the only behaviour change in the initiative and is deliberately second-to-last, so reverting it restores the current always-says-Saved behaviour while leaving every structural step in place. No data migration, no persisted-format change, no wire-protocol change, no feature flag: S16 keeps the exact localStorage and WS formats because the serializers are unchanged, and nothing else alters what is written or sent — so a revert at any point leaves stored shows, song libraries and server state readable by both the old and the new code. The cheap forward-fix for a surface discovered late after a delete step is to re-add that one forwarder as a temporary alias in a one-line commit; the S1 ratchet is what keeps such an alias from silently becoming permanent, because it shows up as an unreviewed addition to EXPECTED_MEMBERS.

open_questions.question: Accessor naming: this plan publishes the collaborators as `store.library` (shows + setlist songs + song library) and `store.arrangement` (sections), because `get shows()` (store.svelte.ts:577, 44 refs) and `get sections()` (:925, 177 refs) are already taken by differently-typed members — a collision both reviewers independently verified and which killed fable's naming outright (publishing under those names makes every array read a type error whose fix is the `store.sections.sections` double-hop). After S9 and S13 delete those forwarders the names ARE free; adopting them would cost one extra mechanical rename pass over ~220 sites, now cheaply gateable by the S8 rename-normalised diff. Keep `library`/`arrangement`, or spend that pass? Same question for `controllerMonitor` versus the terser `monitor`, which would sit beside the unrelated `monitorEvents`/`monitorTypeFilter` app-log cluster.

Is an un-acked WebSocket push evidence of persistence? resilience-hole-0007's proposed fix says show 'Saved' when the local write succeeded OR the server push was delivered — but `client.send` is fire-and-forget with no ack and syncShowToServer early-returns on a closed link (store.svelte.ts:1534-1536), so the web cannot know delivery. S22 takes the conservative default that survived both reviews: 'Saved' iff EVERY local write succeeded, regardless of link state. Accepting that means a user whose localStorage is full sees 'Not saved' even though the server may in fact hold the show. The alternative is adding a server ack to the setShowLibrary/setSongLibrary protocol messages — a protocol change outside this initiative.

This plan deliberately STOPS after publishing the five controllers and does NOT attempt an authoring-document store (graphs/nodes/edges/undo/clipboard). Both reviewers killed sonnet's version of that step — ~3,000 LOC across ~100 files in one commit with no durable resting state and a self-described 'revert wholesale' rollback — and the surviving form is S23's tracked follow-on record with a strangler sub-cluster order. After S23 the store is ~3,250 lines and node/graph authoring, undo, paste, WS link, persistence, transport, backups and OSC/tunnel status still converge on it, i.e. divergent-change-0002 (critical) closes here only partially. Is a ratchet plus a tracked follow-on the right stopping point, or should the follow-on be scheduled as a first-class initiative now?

S18 keeps the Patch routing channel as a field ON the shell object (`shell.patch.routing`) rather than threading a separate object through the view tree. That separates the concern in code without separating it in the dependency graph — components still reach it through the shell. Is the legibility win enough, or should PatchGraphView and the Patch inspector receive the channel as their own prop?

Once the forwarders are gone and S14 has given every *ControllerHost a second, store-free implementation, do the narrow injected Host interfaces stay as they are, or should each controller instead take the owning store as `this`? This plan KEEPS them exported and keeps the `satisfies` checks at store.svelte.ts:397/:538 — un-exporting them was attacked successfully as trading real static shape checking for an export-count cosmetic. Collapsing them further is a separate architecture call and not attempted here.

S1's ratchet needs a strictness decision: does EXPECTED_MEMBERS assert exact deep-equality (every added member is a deliberate, reviewed diff) or only a count cap (cheaper to live with, weaker signal)? This plan assumes exact equality plus a count cap plus a LOC cap; the implementer should confirm the exact-equality list stays maintainable across the five deletion commits rather than degenerating into a rubber stamp, and should seed all three values from what the instrument MEASURES at HEAD rather than from this plan's pre-measured 397/3,630.

synthesis_inputs.rationale: SKELETON: opus, unchanged in shape. It scored highest with both reviewers (4/4/5/4/4 from fable, 4/5/5/5/4 from opus) and is the only variant whose sequencing survived attack: the add-accessor -> migrate-production -> migrate-tests -> delete strangler leaves a shippable tree after every commit, which is exactly what killed sonnet's S10 and what fable's five mixed production+test commits lacked. REPAIRS FORCED BY LANDED ATTACKS ON THE SKELETON: (1) S1 now constructs `new TriggerLab(fakeClient)` — the default constructor at store.svelte.ts:876-879 opens a real WSClient, so the instrument the entire parity story hangs off would have been the one network-touching test in the suite. (2) S4's 'zero store-internal uses' precondition is struck as false; the five genuine internal uses (:979, :1016, :1065, :1078, :1467) are enumerated as must-not-move, and the 6-vs-7 forwarder discrepancy is reconciled by direct measurement — 11 `this.midi.` hits, 6 of them forwarder bodies, which also corrects the attacking reviewer's own tally (it counted :1915/:1919 as internal uses when they are the startMidiLearn/cancelMidiLearn bodies). (3) The diff-shape gate on every test-retarget commit is replaced wholesale: both reviewers landed on it, opus's S12 form could never pass (removed lines contain the OLD path and match no `store\.library\.` filter) and fable's form could never fail on a weakened assertion (the substring whitelist passes the whole line). Both repairs converge on a rename-normalised diff, so that is what S5/S8/S12 use, with a bite-proof before it is trusted. (4) S22 gates `saved()` on ALL local writes rather than 'at least one' — the partial-loss hole where a song-library quota failure beside a successful show write still shows 'Saved' — and adds the mixed-result test case. (5) S23 emits a real follow-on artifact instead of a test-file header comment, so divergent-change-0002 does not close with no owner. GRAFTS FROM RIVALS WHERE THE SKELETON'S VERSION WAS ATTACKED AND THEIRS SURVIVED: sonnet's local-write-only save rule (its S4 was the only autosave step to survive the unacked-push attack intact) is taken over opus's quantifier; sonnet's AuthoringStore ambition survives only as S23's follow-on record with the strangler sub-cluster order both reviewers named as the repair; sonnet's Host-collapse question is carried as open_questions[4]. DROPPED BECAUSE BOTH REVIEWERS BROKE THEM: sonnet's DeviceLinkStore/LibraryStore facades (new one-construction-site classes with no behaviour — the very defect the initiative exists to fix, with an extra dot per call); sonnet's S10 as an executable step; sonnet's naming indecision and its undirected INIT-01/INIT-06 dependency edges; fable's *Host un-exports (store.svelte.ts:397/:538 `satisfies`-check them — verified), fable's same-named getters beside surviving private fields (duplicate class member = compile error), fable's canConnect/canReconnect deletion (53 test call sites churned alongside a transposition), fable's `toPort?: string` (must be `ToPort`), fable's link-open OR-gate, and fable's 1,050 LOC estimate. ADDED BY SYNTHESIS: S14, which is the only constructive answer left to the Host half of speculative-generality-0001 once un-exporting is off the table — give each Host a second, store-free implementation and prove it with `rg -n 'TriggerLab'` returning nothing in that file, turning a hypothetical seam into a used one. RESOLVED (owner=synthesis in opus's variant): the cross-initiative ordering question. dependencies_on_other_initiatives is empty and INIT-02 lands FIRST relative to INIT-06-graph-node-type-model (whose NodeKind redesign collides with graph-wiring.ts:20 `directionOk`) and INIT-09-ui-component-dedup (whose ControllerStatusPanel split collides with PatchControllerInspector.svelte, the file S3/S5 retarget most heavily) — because this initiative's edits are mechanical accessor renames that a later structural change rebases over cleanly, while a structural change rebased under a 580-site rename is not. Phase 10 should encode that direction in its ranking.
